title: STAR-Clarify: A Role-Ambiguity Benchmark and a Clarification Skill for Language Models
content: A reasoning prompt can state a number without stating what the number is: "the lift carries 34 people" gives a capacity or a head count. We call this the role of a value: what the value stands for in the world the prompt describes. We introduce STAR-Clarify, a benchmark of 396 prompts generated from declared worlds. The expected behavior of each prompt (answer, ask, or report an impossibility) is set by its construction, and the answer under each reading is computed. About half of the prompts are clear, so that asking about everything is penalized. We also describe a short skill, built on the categories Things, States, Actions and Relationships (STAR), that asks a model to declare the world of a prompt before reasoning. On the ambiguous prompts, Claude Opus 5.5 resolves 20% silently and Qwen3-30B-A3B 65%. With the skill these shares fall to 0% and 13%. A control prompt that only tells the model to state its reading, without STAR, removes most of the silent resolutions on one-step prompts (24% remain). The skill keeps its advantage where the role of a value is open, including on verbs it never names. Inside a planning problem it removes an error on clear wording, in which the model plans with a stated capacity as if it were an amount (23 of 30 prompts without the skill, 0 with it). Asked to judge the wording, the smaller model calls 80% of the prompts it resolved silently unclear: it notices most of these problems and does not report them when it solves.
